answer: Agents post a signed “willow” token each epoch, then each grader streams its vote into a cryptographic thread that is hashed into a river‑wide ledger. Every epoch the system computes mutual information between graders’ vote vectors; panels whose information exceeds a threshold are flagged and their tokens are burned, forcing each grader to lock up a stake of 10 tokens per identity. An attacker must therefore spend 10 tokens and wait a full epoch for each fake identity, making a Sybil attack cost‑prohibitive.
